name: lance-gg/lance
description: A real-time multiplayer game server framework for Node.js that handles network synchronization, lag compensation, and physics prediction so developers can focus on game logic.
score_rationale: 1.7k stars, solid JavaScript-native multiplayer server library with good documentation and example games.

name: TaloDev/backend
description: A self-hostable game backend providing player authentication, leaderboards, stats, cloud saves, event tracking, and peer-to-peer multiplayer with Godot and Unity plugins.
score_rationale: 86 stars but actively maintained through March 2026 with a clean feature set covering the most common indie game backend needs.

name: wolfpld/tracy
description: A real-time, nanosecond-resolution, remote telemetry, hybrid frame and sampling profiler for games and applications. Supports CPU, GPU (OpenGL, Vulkan, D3D, Metal, CUDA), memory, and context switch profiling.
score_rationale: 15.5k stars, industry-standard game profiler used by AAA and indie studios, supports virtually all major GPU APIs and languages.

name: baldurk/renderdoc
description: A stand-alone frame-capture based graphics debugger supporting Vulkan, D3D11, D3D12, OpenGL, and OpenGL ES on Windows, Linux, Android, and Nintendo Switch. Essential tool for GPU debugging.
score_rationale: 10.5k stars, MIT license, the go-to open-source graphics debugger for game developers across all major graphics APIs.

name: AirtestProject/Airtest
description: A cross-platform UI automation framework for games and apps using image recognition to locate UI elements without code injection. Supports Android, iOS, Windows, and multiple game engines.
score_rationale: 9.2k stars, Apache-2.0, widely adopted mobile game testing framework backed by NetEase with active maintenance.

name: bombomby/optick
description: A super-lightweight C++ profiler for games providing instrumentation, context switching, sampling, and GPU counters. Features a standalone viewer and supports Direct3D 12 and Vulkan GPU profiling.
score_rationale: 3.1k stars, MIT, popular lightweight game profiler used in commercial engines with good cross-platform support.

name: game-ci/unity-builder
description: A GitHub Action for building Unity projects for multiple platforms as part of automated CI/CD pipelines. Part of the GameCI open source initiative for game development automation.
score_rationale: 1k stars, MIT, the standard open-source GitHub Action for automated Unity game builds used by thousands of Unity developers.

name: Tencent/GAutomator
description: An open-source test automation framework for mobile games that interacts with Unity/Unreal engine GameObjects directly, avoiding device resolution adaptation issues across Android and iOS devices.
score_rationale: 1.4k stars, engine-level game automation from Tencent, uniquely targeting GameObject API for robust mobile game testing.

name: EmbarkStudios/puffin
description: A friendly lightweight instrumentation profiler for Rust games and applications, featuring flamegraph visualization, remote profiling over TCP, and egui integration for in-game performance monitoring.
score_rationale: 1.7k stars, dual Apache-2.0/MIT, the primary profiling tool for Rust game development used in production by Embark Studios.

name: game-ci/unity-test-runner
description: A GitHub Action that runs PlayMode and EditMode tests for Unity projects as part of automated CI pipelines. Part of the GameCI open source project.
score_rationale: 247 stars, MIT, widely-used CI tool that enables automated testing of Unity games in GitHub Actions workflows.

name: getsentry/sentry-native
description: The Sentry SDK for C, C++, and native applications providing error and crash reporting with support for Crashpad and Breakpad backends. Useful for native game crash reporting.
score_rationale: 527 stars, MIT, the standard native crash reporting SDK used to integrate Sentry into C/C++ game codebases.

name: AlSch092/UltimateAntiCheat
description: An educational open-source usermode anti-cheat framework for Windows games in C++, detecting and preventing common attack vectors including memory manipulation and DLL injection. Supports optional kernel-mode integration.
score_rationale: 589 stars, AGPL-3.0, useful reference implementation for understanding anti-cheat techniques in game security research.

name: zeux/microprofile
description: An embeddable CPU/GPU profiler with in-app and HTML visualizers supporting hierarchical timing regions and multiple GPU APIs (D3D11/D3D12/OpenGL/Vulkan). Archived but widely referenced.
score_rationale: 495 stars, archived in 2023 but historically significant embeddable game profiler referenced in many game engines.

name: gwaredd/unium
description: A Unity library for game automation that exposes an HTTP API to enable external tools and test scripts to inspect and control game scenes at runtime via a built-in web server.
score_rationale: 238 stars, MIT, niche but unique approach to Unity test automation; last active 2022 suggests limited ongoing development.

name: lrq3000/oacs
description: An open-source Python/ML framework for developing server-side anti-cheating systems, originally built for anomaly detection in real-time games using machine learning algorithms.
score_rationale: 29 stars, research-grade proof-of-concept ML anti-cheat framework with limited adoption and unclear maintenance status.

name: raysan5/raylib
description: A simple and easy-to-use C library for videogames programming, with no external dependencies and support for Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and WebAssembly. Widely adopted for education, prototyping, and indie game development.
score_rationale: Industry-standard beginner-to-intermediate game library with 31k+ stars, extremely active maintenance, and ubiquitous community adoption.

name: 4ian/GDevelop
description: Full-featured, no-code open-source 2D/3D game engine with an event-based visual editor, targeting mobile, desktop, and web. Actively developed with AI-assisted features and a large community.
score_rationale: 21k+ stars, regular releases, and one of the most accessible open-source 2D/3D engines with a powerful visual editor.

name: libgdx/libgdx
description: A Java cross-platform game development framework supporting Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, HTML5, and iOS. Powers many commercial and indie games with a comprehensive API and broad community.
score_rationale: 24.9k stars, Apache-2.0, widely used in production Java game development across all major platforms.

name: cocos2d/cocos2d-x
description: A C++ multi-platform 2D game framework used by millions of developers globally, supporting iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux. Foundation for Cocos Creator engine.
score_rationale: 19k stars, MIT license, industry-proven C++ engine with massive global developer base especially in mobile gaming.

name: MonoGame/MonoGame
description: A .NET/C# cross-platform game framework, the open-source successor to Microsoft's XNA. Powers commercial hits like Celeste and Stardew Valley across desktop, mobile, and console.
score_rationale: 13.3k stars, proven in commercial production with AAA-quality indie titles, broad platform support.

name: hajimehoshi/ebiten
description: A dead simple 2D game engine for Go with a clean API, supporting Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, and WebAssembly. Actively maintained with a growing ecosystem.
score_rationale: 13.1k stars, Apache-2.0, the de facto standard 2D game engine for the Go programming language.

name: love2d/love
description: LOVE is a free, open-source 2D game framework using Lua, supporting Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and iOS. Known for its simplicity, portability, and active game-jam community.
score_rationale: 7.9k stars with a dedicated community; Lua-based framework widely used in game jams and indie development.

name: melonjs/melonJS
description: A fresh, modern, lightweight HTML5 2D game engine with a Canvas2D-inspired API built in JavaScript/TypeScript. Actively maintained with good documentation.
score_rationale: 6.3k stars, MIT, actively maintained HTML5 engine with modern API and solid feature set for web games.

name: defold/defold
description: A completely free cross-platform game engine for desktop, mobile, and web games, using Lua scripting with native extension support. Backed by the Defold Foundation.
score_rationale: 5.9k stars, developer-friendly Apache-derived license, production-proven engine with strong 2D capabilities and active community.

name: AlmasB/FXGL
description: A Java/JavaFX/Kotlin 2D game development framework with a clean API, Entity-Component architecture, animations, and particle systems. Supports Windows, Mac, Linux, Android, iOS, and web.
score_rationale: 4.8k stars, MIT, actively maintained Java/Kotlin engine offering a modern alternative to LibGDX for JVM developers.

name: KilledByAPixel/LittleJS
description: Tiny, fast HTML5 JavaScript game engine with no dependencies, featuring WebGL2+Canvas2D rendering, physics, particles, sound, and input handling. Optimized for js13k and game jams.
score_rationale: 4.1k stars, MIT, highly regarded minimal JS engine popular in game jams with a strong feature-to-size ratio.

name: amzeratul/halley
description: A lightweight C++17 game engine used to ship Wargroove commercially on PC, Mac, Nintendo Switch, Xbox One, and PS4. Features ECS architecture and modern tooling.
score_rationale: 3.8k stars, Apache-2.0, commercially proven C++ engine with ECS and cross-platform console support.

name: pygame/pygame
description: A free, open-source Python library for multimedia and game development built on SDL, providing graphics, sound, input, and sprite management. The standard Python game development library.
score_rationale: 8.7k stars, the canonical Python game development library used worldwide in education and indie game development.

name: pythonarcade/arcade
description: Easy to use Python library for creating 2D arcade games, built atop pyglet and OpenGL. Designed for beginners and educators with clean modern API.
score_rationale: 2k stars, MIT, modern Python alternative to pygame with cleaner API and active educational community.

name: HaxeFlixel/flixel
description: Free, cross-platform 2D game engine powered by Haxe and OpenFL, enabling native and web deployment from a single codebase. Inspired by ActionScript Flixel.
score_rationale: 2.2k stars, MIT, the primary 2D game engine for Haxe with strong cross-platform capabilities and active use in indie games.
